summary.headline: Beat estimates 8 quarters straight, but analysts are cutting longer-term forecasts
summary.takeaway: Apple beat profit estimates in all of the last 8 quarters. However, the share price often fell the day after, and analysts have recently cut more estimates than they raised for most future periods.

positives.text: EPS (profit per share) beat Wall Street estimates in 8 of the last 8 quarters, by between 1.7% and 9.5%.
The latest quarter (Q4 FY26) showed EPS of $2.10 against a $1.98 estimate, a 5.8% beat.
For the current quarter, 11 analysts raised estimates and 4 cut them in the last 30 days.

watch_outs.text: Beats did not always lift the price. After Q3 FY26 the stock fell 7.35% the next day despite a 6.7% beat.
For the current fiscal year, 23 analysts cut estimates and only 7 raised them in the last 30 days.
Next-quarter and next-fiscal-year estimates also saw more cuts than raises: 13 vs 2 and 10 vs 3.

what_to_watch_next: Next earnings around 28 Jan 2027 after market close. 25 Wall Street analysts estimate EPS of $2.91 (vs $2.84 a year ago) and revenue of $156 billion.
The stock has typically moved about 2.4% up or down the day after earnings.
